title: Migrations do not reproduce prod's grants — a DB built from migrations serves no data
description:
A database built from `supabase/migrations` alone does not serve traffic: `anon` cannot SELECT `public.occurrences`, and the REST API answers `permission denied for view occurrences`.

Found 2026-07-30 while mirroring prod into the local stack.

## Evidence

SELECT grants to `anon`/`authenticated` on `public` + `dwc`:

- **prod: 48**
- **fresh `supabase db reset` from migrations: 14**

**34 grants exist only in prod** — 17 relations x 2 roles. The migrations-only set is a strict subset of prod's; nothing is granted locally that prod lacks. They cover essentially the whole public API surface: `occurrences`, `contributors`, `individuals`, `designations`, `observations`, `observation_photos`, `identifications`, `parties`, `social_groups`, `group_memberships`, `providers`, `collections`, `organizations`, `user_contributor`, `contributor_email_addresses`, `occurrence_identifications`, `occurrence_unresolved_codes`.

(An earlier revision of this issue said 15 and 33. That was an artifact of psql's `Time:` output being captured into the comparison file, inflating the local count by one. Corrected 2026-07-30 after CodeRabbit flagged the arithmetic on PR #356.)

`grep -rn "GRANT.*occurrences" supabase/migrations/` finds grants for `individual_occurrences`, `group_occurrences` and `ecotype_occurrences` -- but **never for `public.occurrences` itself**.

## Why it has gone unnoticed

The grants were applied to prod out of band. Every later migration touches the view with `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW`, which **preserves existing grants** -- so nothing ever disturbed them in prod, and nothing ever recreated them anywhere else.

This directly violates the convention already written in CLAUDE.md: "SELECT grants ship in the same migration that creates a table (Supabase RLS defaults silently zero out joins otherwise)."

## Impact

- Prod cannot be rebuilt from migrations. If it ever had to be (disaster recovery, a new environment, a staging clone), the frontend would come up dead.
- Local dev and CI are not representative. Anything exercising the anon REST path against a freshly reset DB tests a different permission model than prod.
- The gap is invisible from prod, which is the only place that looks correct.

## NOT a security problem

`contributor_email_addresses` is granted to `anon` in prod, but it has RLS enabled with **zero policies** -- default-deny, so `anon` gets no rows. Checked `contributors` (RLS, 1 policy), `user_contributor` (RLS, 1 policy), `observations` (RLS, 3 policies). No leak. The issue is reproducibility, not exposure.

## Fix

PR #356 — migration `20260730120000_public_select_grants.sql`. Verified: a fresh reset now yields grants byte-identical to prod (48 = 48, empty diff both directions), and `/rest/v1/occurrences` returns `[]` with the anon key.
acceptance_criteria:
- A migration adds every SELECT grant prod has and migrations lack, so `supabase db reset` produces a database whose anon/authenticated grants match prod exactly (48 = 48, empty diff in both directions).
- After a bare `supabase db reset`, `/rest/v1/occurrences` with the anon key returns HTTP 200 and a well-formed result — `[]` on an unseeded reset, rows when data is present — rather than the `permission denied for view occurrences` error it returned before. The check is on the permission path, not on row count.
- A guard exists against regressing: either a CI assertion diffing grants against a checked-in expected set, or a smoke test hitting the anon REST path on the freshly reset CI database.
- The other two drift items found alongside this are recorded (see notes) and either fixed or explicitly accepted.
notes:
Two smaller drifts found in the same sweep. A full column-level diff (389 columns each side) showed ONLY these:

1. `happywhale.encounter_sample` -- exists in prod, no migration creates it. One `id integer` column, 5,610 rows, referenced nowhere in the repo. Looks like an ad-hoc sampling leftover. Decide: drop it in prod, or add a migration.
2. `happywhale.individuals.primary_id` and `.nickname` are `varchar(100)` in prod; migrations declare `varchar(50)`. Only `nickname` needs it (2 rows over 50 chars, max 60); `primary_id` maxes at 28. Note `public.occurrences` depends on `primary_id`, so widening it in a migration means dropping and recreating the view -- `ALTER TABLE` alone fails with "cannot alter type of a column used by a view or rule".

`scripts/pull-prod-db.sh` (PR #355) works around both -- excludes the table, widens `nickname`. Those workarounds should be deleted as each drift is reconciled in a migration. The grant replay step in that script is now redundant with migration 20260730120000 but is kept as a guard against future out-of-band drift.

Related: salish-6j6 covers revoking the inert anon/authenticated write grants and the `contributor_email_addresses` SELECT grant.

Reproduce the grant diff:
```
supabase db reset --no-seed
# then diff information_schema.role_table_grants for
# table_schema in ('public','dwc'), grantee in ('anon','authenticated'),
# privilege_type='SELECT'  -- prod vs local
# NB: run psql with timing OFF, or '\timing' output lands in the file and
# inflates the count by one. That artifact caused the original 15/33 figures.
```

title: iNaturalist ingest fails intermittently on live-window pagination drift (SALISHSEA-IO-2D)
description: Sentry SALISHSEA-IO-2D (escalating, ~25 events/2d, ~4% of the */5 cron runs): fetchAllObservationPages throws 'iNaturalist pagination incomplete: fetched N page(s) for total_results=X'. Root cause: the ingest window ends at current_date (today), so the dataset mutates between sequential page-number requests. total_results drifts or per-page counts stop summing to it, and isPaginationComplete (correctly) refuses the snapshot. Reproduced against the live v2/observations API. Fix: re-page the whole window a bounded number of times (transient, self-heals on a fresh pass) before throwing; keep the pure completeness invariant unchanged. Durable follow-up: switch to id-keyset pagination (order_by=id&id_above) which is atomic over a live tail and sidesteps the 10k page cap.
design: Bounded whole-fetch retry in the shell (fetch-inaturalist.ts), reusing retry.ts backoff. Only isPaginationComplete==false triggers re-page; parse/HTTP/cap errors still abort immediately per decision 011.
notes: PR #327 (branch ingest/inat-pagination-drift-retry) — bounded whole-window re-page. Awaiting CodeRabbit review before merge. Not deployed until merged to main (deploy.yml runs 'supabase functions deploy ingest').
close_reason: Fixed in PR #327, merged to main and deployed to prod (supabase functions deploy ingest succeeded, run 29068586608). Bounded whole-window re-page on pagination drift. Follow-up (id-keyset pagination) tracked separately.

title: occurrence_index matview: cheap timestamp/location lookup for stored claims
description: The occurrences view is a 4-way UNION with no usable index on its computed id, so joining it materializes the whole thing whenever consumed unfiltered. Today group_occurrences/individual_occurrences avoid this only because their stored-identifications branch has an empty outer (0 curator claims). The moment curation adds rows, even the filtered per-subject pages degrade, and ecotype_occurrences can't include stored claims at all (it dropped that branch to fix a prod timeout — decision 017 / migration 20260708040216). Fix: a small MATERIALIZED VIEW occurrence_index (id PK, observed_at, location) over public.occurrences, unique-indexed on id, refreshed on the same cron tick as occurrence_identifier_candidates. Repoint all stored-claims branches to join occurrence_index instead of occurrences. Prerequisite for the curation UI.
close_reason: occurrence_index matview shipped in PR #326 / migration 20260708052333; all stored-claims branches repointed, ecotype aggregate regained stored claims

Today supabase/functions/ingest/index.ts falls back to SUPABASE_DB_URL (superuser). Create an 'ingest' login role with only the grants the shell needs (mirror schemas maplify/inaturalist, ingest.runs, taxa lookup), set its password out-of-band, set INGEST_DB_URL in Edge Function secrets, verify a cron run succeeds under the new role, then remove/rotate the superuser fallback.

Verified: prod dry-runs of both sources OK under the role, pg_stat_activity shows usename=ingest, cron runs #28/#29 success post-flip. Superuser fallback removal split to a follow-up issue.

title: Cutover: switch pg_cron from SQL ingest to the Edge Function; remove SQL ingest path
description: Clean atomic cutover per decision 011. One migration: schedule pg_net invocation of the ingest Edge Function (Maplify + iNat) AND cron.unschedule the old load-recent-maplify-sightings / load-recent-inaturalist-observations jobs together — never two live reconcilers. Downtime acceptable (10-day windows self-heal on first new run). Validate via manual dry-run against real windows before flipping. After bake-in, remove the now-dead in-DB HTTP fetch functions (fetch_date_range, fetch_observation_page, update_sightings/update_observations HTTP paths, ensure_taxa/fetch_taxa) — Postgres keeps only storage + the pure relational views. Rollback = single migration revert.
acceptance_criteria: pg_cron invokes the Edge Function; old SQL cron jobs unscheduled in the same migration; dead in-DB HTTP fetch functions removed; live map unaffected after cutover; rollback path documented.
notes:
CUTOVER LIVE + confirmed healthy (2026-07-06). #308 merged; deploy failed once on transient Supabase link OOM (fail-safe: cron stayed on SQL), succeeded on rerun. Prod cron switched to pg_net jobs (SQL load-recent-* gone). ISSUE: pg_net not installed in prod (local stack pre-enables it) → cron failed 'schema net does not exist' ~15:00-15:10; ingest briefly down (self-healing). FIX: enabled pg_net in prod out-of-band + codified in migration 20260706120000 (PR #309). Confirmed: both sources cron-driven success in ingest.runs (maplify 277/282, inat 413), all net._http_response 200. First iNat run reconciled -17 obs (one-time drift convergence, expected). Lesson saved to memory (local-prod-extension-parity). REMAINING: retirement migration only (#309 merged; 89d.4 heartbeat shipped in #310).

BAKE-IN PLAN (2026-07-06): heartbeat (89d.4) merged + verified end-to-end; retirement migration (drop dead SQL ingest fns) intentionally deferred to ~2026-07-13 so the SQL path remains restorable during bake-in. Dedicated ingest role split to salish-wco; Sentry split to salish-vif.
RETIREMENT SHIPPED 2026-07-31 (PR pending): migration 20260731120000 drops the 9 dead Maplify/iNaturalist in-DB functions. Verified against prod first — closed dependency cluster, no cron, no triggers, Edge Function uses raw SQL and calls none of them. HappyWhale's 3 HTTP functions deliberately excluded (never part of this cutover, no ingest.runs rows, no TS replacement) — split to salish-mzz. seed.sql emptied: it called three of the dropped functions and made CI hit live third-party APIs on every build.

title: iNaturalist ingest: pagination + full taxon-closure resolution
description: Extend the ingest skeleton to iNaturalist, reusing the Maplify shell/core. Adds the two hard pieces: (1) pagination-completeness — fetch every page through total_results; any page failure aborts (write nothing); an empty first page (total_results=0) is complete/authoritative. (2) taxon resolution moved into TS: extract referenced taxon+ancestor ids (pure), diff against inaturalist.taxa (pure), shell loops fetch->recompute-still-missing until the full ancestor closure resolves, ALL before opening the persist txn (no HTTP inside the DB write). A taxon-API failure counts against fetch-completeness. Persist observations + observation_photos (parent/child) + taxa in one atomic txn with guarded reconcile. Implements decision 011 for iNaturalist.
acceptance_criteria: All in-scope observations in a window are ingested regardless of count; taxon FK never dangles; a partial page fetch or taxon-API failure writes nothing; vitest covers the completeness predicate, taxon-closure diff, and pagination; integration test proves observation+photo persist + reconcile bounds.
notes: Shell implemented: supabase/functions/ingest/fetch-inaturalist.ts (pagination + taxon-closure loops), index.ts branches on source. persist.ts toPhotoPayload now dedupes photos by id (live iNat shares a photo id across observations → bulk ON CONFLICT crash; caught by live run). PR #307. Live-validated: 42-page dry run (8269 results), real write, closure loop re-fetched a deleted taxon, failure paths. 283 tests green.
close_reason: Both slices merged: core+persist (#306) and Edge Function shell (#307). iNaturalist ingest runs end-to-end via the Edge Function — pagination loop + taxon-closure loop, live-validated against the real API. A third live-run bug caught (photo id reused across observations). Follow-up 1wz (fetch-maplify timeout tidy). Remaining in epic: 89d.3 cutover + deferred 89d.1 follow-ups (ingest role, Sentry).

title: Ingest skeleton + Maplify: imperative shell / functional core
description: Build the reusable ingest skeleton and prove it end-to-end on Maplify (simplest source: single-shot fetch, no pagination, no taxon graph). Deliverables: (1) functional core in scripts/ingest/ (Maplify JSON -> normalized sighting rows, coordinate parsing, reconcile diff, completeness predicate) with vitest unit tests; (2) Deno imperative shell in supabase/functions/ingest/ (fetch + minimal retry honoring Retry-After, structured console logs, Sentry Deno, dedicated-role pooled PG connection, one atomic txn: upserts + guarded reconcile DELETE bounded to window); (3) ingest_runs audit table + writes outside the data txn; (4) INGEST_TRIGGER_SECRET auth; (5) manual/dry-run invocation interface (source+window+dry_run); (6) vitest integration test on local Supabase proving reconcile touches ONLY in-window rows, upsert idempotency, abort-writes-nothing. Implements decision 011 for Maplify. Completeness invariant: non-200/error aborts and writes nothing; empty-200 reconciles authoritatively.
acceptance_criteria: Maplify ingest runs as an Edge Function on the same 5-min cadence; a failed/empty-error fetch leaves existing sightings intact; an empty-200 reconciles the window; manual re-fetch and dry-run work; ingest_runs records every run; vitest unit+integration green in CI.
notes: Slice 3 (Deno Edge Function shell) done → PR #305. supabase/functions/ingest/ (index.ts orchestration + fetch-maplify.ts retry + deno.json import map); scripts/ingest/retry.ts (pure, tested); fetchWindowIds on persist; config.toml [functions.ingest] verify_jwt=false. Live bug caught+fixed: Maplify count is a STRING not number (schema dropped count, fixture made faithful, regression test). Validated live: 401 bad secret, 405 inaturalist, dry-run (97/0 nothing written), real run idempotent, ingest.runs records success+failure. 237 tests green, deno check + tsc clean. Function is DORMANT (deploy.yml doesn't run functions deploy). FOLLOW-UPS: dedicated ingest DB role+grants (shell prefers INGEST_DB_URL); Sentry Deno wiring; then 89d.2 iNat, 89d.3 cutover (deploy fn + pg_cron→pg_net).

title: Deploy pipeline has no test gate, no rollback, and no failure alerting
description:
deploy.yml on push to main runs only 'npm run build' (deploy.yml:35). Tests, e2e, and the type-drift check live only in build.yml on pull_request, so: (a) the merge commit on main is never tested before deploy (PR checks run on the PR head, not the merge result); (b) any push reaching main outside a passing-PR path deploys with zero test verification. The deploy then runs supabase db push -> S3 sync -> CloudFront invalidation -> cdk deploy in sequence with no atomicity and no rollback — a mid-sequence failure leaves DB schema ahead of a stale frontend, or a new frontend against an old edge handler. smoke.yml runs AFTER deploy via workflow_run and only turns the run red — no alert, no issue filed.

Fix: add a test/e2e/type-drift gate to the deploy path (or enforce required PR checks + test the merge result); add post-deploy verification inside the deploy job with failure alerting; consider aligning to the dwca-nightly.yml pattern (concurrency, post-publish verify, auto-filed failure issues), which already does this well.
acceptance_criteria: A broken build cannot reach prod without a failing gate; deploy failures produce an alert/issue; post-deploy smoke gates or auto-reverts on failure.

title: Reconcile DwC-A go-live with its documented rights preconditions; record a go-live decision
description:
The public DwC-A download link is live (about.html), but two documented preconditions appear unmet and unrecorded:
1) rights-policy.md §1.3 (D-08) requires an explicit notice on the submission form that the observation will be published under CC-BY-NC 4.0 in a DarwinCore Archive, BEFORE the link goes live. src/sighting-form.ts only handles a PHOTO license choice — no observation-publication notice exists.
2) rights-policy.md §4.5 defines a hold requiring a Maplify data-QA pass and a 2-4 week courtesy-notification window to Conserve.IO / Orca Network / Cascadia before exit. No decision record documents the hold was exited, QA passed, or notifications sent.

This is a trust/legal item. Action: add the consent notice to the submission form; reconcile whether the hold conditions were actually met; write a numbered decision record (docs/decisions/) documenting the go-live and closing D-07/D-08. See product/docs audit.
acceptance_criteria: Submission form carries the CC-BY-NC 4.0 / DwC-A publication notice; a decision record documents go-live and the state of the §4.5 hold conditions; D-07 and D-08 closed in rights-policy.md.

title: iNaturalist ingest only fetches page 1 (200 records) — silent truncation
description:
inaturalist.update_observations calls fetch_observation_page(from, to, bbox, taxa, 1, 200) with no pagination loop (supabase/migrations/20260526000000_inat_add_lutrinae.sql:6-13) and ignores the total_results the function already exposes (20260621010000_inat_orcid_capture.sql:44). Any 10-day window with >200 in-scope observations silently drops the overflow. Latent at current volume but an unguarded correctness cliff, and higher risk now that taxonomic scope expanded to all marine mammals (decision 009 added Lutrinae).

VERIFIED against source. Fix in-place: loop pages until fetched >= total_results (or last page empty). Superseded long-term by the TS ingest migration (salish-89d).
acceptance_criteria: All in-scope observations in the window are ingested regardless of count; pagination continues until total_results is satisfied.
close_reason: Fixed in-place: inaturalist.update_observations now paginates through total_results instead of fetching only page 1 (migration 20260705120000). Verified via mock: 450 results → 3 pages/450 rows; empty window → 0 upserts; exactly-200 → 1 page (no infinite loop). Superseded long-term by salish-89d.

title: Maplify ingest deletes ~10 days of live sightings on any failed/empty upstream fetch
description:
maplify.update_sightings runs every 5 minutes over current_date-10..current_date (supabase/migrations/20250914232212_cron.sql:159). Its MERGE ends with 'WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE AND s.created_at BETWEEN $1 AND ($2+1) THEN DELETE' (supabase/migrations/20260620000200_resolution_ingest.sql:141-143). The MERGE source is maplify.fetch_date_range, filtered 'WHERE status = 200' (20250904165159_fetch_data.sql:186). Any non-200 (500/403/rate-limit) or a 200 with an empty results array yields ZERO source rows, so every sighting in the 10-day window becomes NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE and is DELETED. Runs every 5 min, so a transient Maplify outage repeatedly wipes ~10 days of sightings from the live map until Maplify recovers. Self-heals on next good fetch; the nightly export row-floor guard prevents a near-empty archive, so damage is to the live site, not the DwC-A.

VERIFIED against source. The older BEGIN ATOMIC definition (fetch_data.sql) has the same flaw (unconditional DELETE then INSERT).

Fix: guard the reconciliation/DELETE on a confirmed successful, non-empty fetch — distinguish 'upstream returned no rows' (do nothing / skip delete) from 'upstream genuinely removed these rows'. Superseded long-term by the TS ingest migration (salish-89d), but fix in-place now.
acceptance_criteria: A failed or empty Maplify fetch leaves existing sightings intact; DELETE only occurs when the fetch demonstrably succeeded and returned the authoritative set for the window.
close_reason: Fixed in-place: maplify.update_sightings now guards the reconcile DELETE on a successful, non-empty fetch (migration 20260705120000). Verified via mock-based transactional test — failed/empty fetch leaves sightings intact (2 survivors each); a good fetch still reconciles (update/insert/delete-absent). Superseded long-term by salish-89d.

title: Migrate network ingest from Postgres into a TypeScript imperative shell / functional core
description:
Today all external network ingest (Maplify, iNaturalist) runs INSIDE Postgres: pg_cron schedules SQL functions that use the http extension to fetch upstream JSON and MERGE it into tables (supabase/migrations/20250914232212_cron.sql, 20250904165159_fetch_data.sql, 20260620000200_resolution_ingest.sql). This concentrates network I/O, control flow, taxon mapping, dedup, and destructive writes in an environment with no exception handling, no structured logging, no retry/backoff, no test harness, and dangerous failure modes (see the Maplify blind-DELETE and iNat single-page bugs filed alongside this epic).

Goal: move network operations into a TypeScript IMPERATIVE SHELL (fetch, retry/backoff, structured logging, Sentry, success-guarded persistence, orchestration) wrapping a FUNCTIONAL RELATIONAL CORE of pure, unit-testable transforms (upstream JSON -> normalized records, taxon mapping, coordinate parsing, dedup, collection resolution). Postgres becomes a store, not an HTTP client. A fetch that fails or returns empty must NEVER be interpreted as 'upstream deleted everything' — writes are guarded on a confirmed successful fetch.

This is a priority architectural direction. The two data-loss bugs are the concrete motivation; fix those in-place first (they are urgent), then this epic supersedes the SQL ingest path entirely.

Scope to define in child issues: runner/host (scheduled GitHub Action vs Supabase Edge Function vs small worker), how state/cron moves off pg_cron, idempotent upsert strategy from TS, and a test suite for the functional core.
design: Imperative shell = effects (fetch, retry, log, persist, schedule). Functional core = pure transforms over plain data, exhaustively unit-tested. Replace blind 'WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE' with reconciliation only after a verified-complete fetch. Structured logs + Sentry breadcrumbs on every ingest run; per-source success/failure/rowcount metrics. Keep Postgres for storage + the pure relational views (occurrences, segments) that are legitimately declarative.
notes: Design resolved via grilling session 2026-07-05 → docs/decisions/011-ingest-imperative-shell.md. Host: Supabase Edge Function (Deno), scheduled by pg_cron+pg_net every 5 min, also a manually-invocable curator endpoint (source+window+dry_run). Persist: direct pooled connection as dedicated ingest role, parameterized SQL in TS, one atomic txn for upserts+reconcile, ingest_runs audit row outside it. Safety invariant: reconcile iff fetch provably complete (all pages + iNat taxon closure); non-200/partial aborts and writes nothing; empty-200 is authoritative. Scope: Maplify then iNat; HappyWhale out (pending integration green light). Retry: minimal in-invocation, honor Retry-After. Auth: dedicated INGEST_TRIGGER_SECRET. Tests: vitest only (unit core + local-Supabase integration for persist/delete-bounds); no pgTAP. Cutover: clean atomic switch, downtime fine (10-day windows self-heal). Core lives in scripts/ingest/ (vitest), shell in supabase/functions/ingest/.

title: Rich preview fails with CloudFront error for shared occurrence links
description: Sharing https://salishsea.io/?o=inaturalist:377539157 to Facebook renders a broken preview: 'ERROR: The request could not be satisfied' (the standard CloudFront error page). This is the Lambda@Edge OG-meta rich-preview path (docs/decisions/002), which is specified to FAIL OPEN (pass through on any error) — so either that regressed or the failure is a Lambda execution error/timeout CloudFront surfaces as 502/504. Hypothesis to check first: breakage is specific to iNaturalist-prefixed occurrence IDs (inaturalist:NNN) — iNat is modeled-but-export-excluded per SRC-01 (decision 005), so the edge lookup may hit a code path that throws instead of failing open. Repro: crawler user-agent (facebookexternalhit) against the ?o= URL.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed, not iNat-specific): the Lambda@Edge handler (infra/lib/edge-handler/index.ts) intercepts crawler requests on ALL paths except its bypass list (/dwca/, /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt — lines 119-125). og:image is https://salishsea.io/preview.jpg (FALLBACK_IMAGE, line 106). When Facebook's crawler fetches that image URL, the handler has no ?o=, so it returns generic OG *HTML* (lines 137-143) instead of the JPEG. Confirmed: /preview.jpg returns image/jpeg 168717B to a browser UA but text/html 896B to facebookexternalhit. Blast radius: every preview whose og:image falls back to preview.jpg — the generic site card AND any occurrence with no open-licensed (cc0/cc-by) photo, which includes this iNat river-otter. Occurrences with an external open photo URL have an off-host og:image and are unaffected, which is why it wasn't universally caught. FIX: add static image assets to the pre-bot bypass so crawlers always get raw asset bytes (e.g. bypass when request.uri matches /\.(jpe?g|png|gif|svg|webp|ico|avif)$/i). Note: index.test.ts lines 94-162 assert og:image==preview.jpg but never assert preview.jpg itself serves an image — add a regression test that a crawler request to /preview.jpg passes through (returns the request, not synthesized HTML).
Fixed via PR #299 (merged to main, deployed by GH Actions run 28626380144, both Build+Deploy green). Verified live 2026-07-02: /preview.jpg returns image/jpeg 168717B to facebookexternalhit (was text/html 896B); occurrence OG HTML still generated correctly; home page still intercepted. Remaining human step: re-scrape shared links in FB Sharing Debugger to bust cache.

title: Expand scope from cetaceans to all Salish Sea marine mammals (PSEMP)
description:
PRODUCT.md and docs/decisions/001 currently scope the platform to cetaceans only; actual intent is all Salish Sea marine mammals per the PSEMP Marine Mammals Workgroup hub (https://psemp-marinemammalsworkgroup-wa-psp.hub.arcgis.com/): cetaceans + pinnipeds (harbor seal, CA/Steller sea lion, N elephant seal) + otters (sea + marine-foraging river otter). The Lutrinae taxon already hand-added to the iNaturalist query is an early instance.

Open decisions (for a grill-with-docs session, not this migration PR):

title: Revoke inert anon/authenticated write grants on public relations
description:
Production grants `anon` and `authenticated` INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on 44 `public` relations. Nothing needs them and no migration created them.

Found 2026-07-30 alongside salish-0ew; deliberately left out of that fix so a parity migration did not also change production's permissions.

## Not a vulnerability

Checked every RLS policy in `public` on 2026-07-30:

- Every table carrying these grants has RLS **enabled**.
- **No policy permits an anon write.** Every anon policy is `FOR SELECT`. The `FOR ALL` policies on `observations` and `observation_photos` are scoped to `authenticated` with ownership predicates (`user_uuid = auth.uid()`, or a contributor-join).
- The remaining relations are views (`occurrences`, `occurrence_days`, `individual_occurrences`, `group_occurrences`, `ecotype_occurrences`, `occurrence_identifications`, `occurrence_unresolved_codes`). They are UNION/aggregate views, so they are not auto-updatable and a write fails regardless of grant.

So the grants are inert. This is cleanup, not an incident.

## Why bother

They are a loaded footgun. The moment someone adds a permissive policy to one of these tables -- entirely reasonable in isolation -- the write grant is already sitting there and the table becomes anon-writable. Defence in depth wants the grant absent, so that a policy mistake alone is not sufficient.

Also included: `GRANT SELECT ON public.contributor_email_addresses TO anon, authenticated`, reproduced in migration `20260730120000` purely to match prod. It is inert today (RLS on, zero policies, default deny) but should not exist.

## The care this needs

`authenticated` genuinely writes to `observations` and `observation_photos` -- the sighting form's path. Revoking too broadly breaks contribution, and the failure would be silent for anonymous readers and loud only for logged-in contributors, so it will not show up in a smoke test that does not log in.

Work out exactly which grants the write paths depend on before revoking anything. `sighting-form.ts` goes through `rpc('upsert_observation')`, which may be SECURITY DEFINER and therefore not need direct table grants at all -- confirm rather than assume, and check the delete and photo-attachment paths too.

Revoke in a migration (so local/CI/prod stay reconciled), not out of band -- out-of-band changes are exactly what caused salish-0ew.
acceptance_criteria:
- The write paths (`upsert_observation`, delete, photo attachment) are traced and documented, establishing which grants `authenticated` actually requires.
- A migration revokes INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from `anon` on all 44 relations, and from `authenticated` on everything the traced paths do not need.
- `SELECT` on `public.contributor_email_addresses` is revoked from `anon` and `authenticated` in the same migration.
- A logged-in contributor can still create, edit and delete a sighting with photos, verified against a database built from migrations.
- Anonymous read of the map, list and calendar is unaffected.

title: Regions filter the data, and shade the map outside the active region
description:
Follow-on to #352 (Go-to place bubbles) and encompassing GH issue #16 ("Shade map area outside the bounds of the data").

## Why

Today the region bubbles are pure navigation: clicking one zooms the map and nothing else changes. Two problems follow.

1. Absence reads as absence. A user who pans past the edge of our ingest coverage sees empty water and concludes there were no whales there, when in fact we carry no data there at all. That is GH #16.
2. The region is not a durable piece of state. Pan away and the framing is gone; there is nothing to share, nothing in the URL, and no way to say "show me Puget Sound" as a question about the data rather than about the viewport.

Promoting regions from viewport presets to a filter fixes both: the region becomes the scope of the query, and the area outside it is shaded to say plainly "we are not showing you anything here."

## What

A selected region filters the occurrence data and masks the map outside itself. It persists across pan and zoom, survives reload, and is shareable.

Salish Sea is the default.
design:
Decided with the user 2026-07-30:

**1. The mask means "the region you selected", not "where our coverage ends."**
One concept, one mask. Picking a region both filters the data and shades everything outside it. Rejected: a separate permanent coverage mask derived from source/taxon extents layered under a lighter region outline (truer to #16's framing, but two overlapping shaded areas to design and caption); and shading the intersection of region and coverage (single mask whose meaning shifts depending on which constraint binds).

**2. Regions stay lon/lat rectangles.**
Reuse the existing `Extent` constants in src/constants.ts. The filter is exact and predictable and this ships without sourcing new geodata. Accepted cost: a rectangle shaded over the Salish Sea is crude -- it clips Puget Sound's south end and includes Vancouver Island's interior. Rejected for now: real polygons (Salish Sea water body, NOAA SRKW critical habitat) -- better-looking and semantically real, but needs sourcing, licensing, simplification and a home (static GeoJSON vs a PostGIS table). Also rejected: bbox filter + polygon mask, which makes the shading and the filter disagree at the edges (points visible inside a shaded corner).

**3. The filter applies to the map, the observation list, AND the calendar's day counts.**
Everything the sidebar shows must agree. If the calendar counted sightings the map is not drawing, a day would read "busy" and click through to empty water -- the exact confusion this issue exists to remove. See the RESOLVED section in the notes: only the calendar needs a schema change; the map and list filter through plain PostgREST.

**4. Every bubble filters.** Puget Sound, Salish Sea, San Juans, SRKW Range -- one control, one meaning. Picking San Juans hides a sighting off Victoria 20 miles away; acceptable because the mask makes the hiding visible. Rejected: coarse regions filter while fine ones only navigate (two visually identical bubbles doing different things).

**5. "Salish Sea" as a filter means `salishSeaExtent` = [-126, 47, -122, 50.5]** -- NOT the `salishSRKWExtent` = [-124, 47, -122, 49.5] the bubble uses today. Settled 2026-07-30, resolving open item (a). The tight SRKW-clipped extent was chosen in #352 to frame "the water the sightings are actually in", which is right for a viewport and wrong for a filter: as the default it would silently drop the Strait of Georgia north of 49.5 and the whole western Strait of Juan de Fuca / Swiftsure Bank west of -124. Implementation note: decide explicitly whether the *zoom* keeps the tight extent while the *filter* uses the wide one, or both widen. Two extents for one bubble needs a comment saying why, or it reads as a bug.

**6. There is an "Everywhere" escape hatch.** Settled 2026-07-30, resolving open item (b). Without it the widest region is SRKW Range [-125.5, 36, -122, 54] while ingest reaches `acartiaExtent` [-136, 36, -120, 54], leaving real data permanently unreachable from the UI. "Everywhere" drops the region filter entirely (and draws no mask). Costs one more bubble in an already-full row -- worth watching at 390px width, where the Go-to row is already the tightest thing in the panel.

**Assumed, not asked:** selecting a region still zooms the map to it, as the bubbles do today. The filter is what is new; the navigation is retained.
acceptance_criteria:
- Selecting a region filters the map features, the sidebar observation list, and the calendar's per-day volume circles, consistently.
- The filter persists across pan, zoom, day changes, reload and back/forward; it is encoded in the URL and a shared link reproduces it.
- The map area outside the active region is visibly shaded, in a treatment that reads as "we are not showing data here", satisfying GH #16.
- Salish Sea is the default on a fresh load with no region in the URL, using `salishSeaExtent` per design decision 5.
- The `occurrence_days` change is verified against prod-scale data: the month predicate still pushes down through the GROUP BY into each UNION branch with the bbox added, and a month still returns within the latency budget decision 021 set (~120-170 ms). NOT an index requirement — prod has no spatial index and this issue explicitly does not add one; see the measurements in the notes.
- Decision record written; docs/decisions/README.md updated; GH #16 closed by the PR.
notes:
Open items to settle during implementation, in rough priority order:

**a. The "Salish Sea" extent is wrong for a filter.** The bubble uses `salishSRKWExtent` = [-124, 47, -122, 49.5], deliberately, because #352 wanted framing on "the water the sightings are actually in". As the DEFAULT FILTER it silently drops real data: everything in the Strait of Georgia north of 49.5, and the whole western Strait of Juan de Fuca / Swiftsure Bank west of -124. `salishSeaExtent` = [-126, 47, -122, 50.5] is the honest choice for filtering. Consider keeping the tight extent for the zoom and the wide one for the filter, or just widening both. Resolve before implementing -- it decides what the default hides.

**b. No escape hatch was chosen.** The widest bubble is SRKW Range [-125.5, 36, -122, 54]; ingest reaches `acartiaExtent` [-136, 36, -120, 54]. With every bubble a filter and no "Everywhere" option, data in that gap becomes unreachable from the UI. Either add an "Everywhere" bubble, or accept and document that the app only ever shows the SRKW range at widest.

**c. URL state.** The region needs a param (`?r=puget-sound` or similar) alongside `d`/`x`/`y`/`z`/`o`, with slugs, validation and a popstate path. See `parseUrlParams`/`setQueryParams` in src/salish-sea.ts.

**d. `?o=` pointing outside the active region.** `hydrateFromOccurrenceId` can land on an occurrence the current filter excludes. Widen the region to fit it, or clear the filter, or refuse -- needs a decision.

**e. Realtime and the sighting form.** The `occurrences_changed` broadcast refetch must carry the region. A contributor can save a sighting outside the active region (the form validates against `acartiaExtent`) and then not see it -- decide whether saving widens or clears the filter.

**f. Mask rendering.** An OpenLayers layer drawing world-minus-region. Needs a treatment that reads as "no data here" rather than "disabled", and must not swallow map interactions or the basemap's own legibility.

**g. Out of scope:** individual/matriline profile page maps, and the DwC-A export.

**h. Write a decision record** for the mask-means-selected-region and rectangles-for-now calls before implementing -- per CLAUDE.md, decisions get written when made.

---

## Measured on prod, 2026-07-30 (corpus: 61,389 occurrences; 39,608 maplify + 20,569 iNat)

Bbox filtering is cheap, but NOT because of an index -- there is no spatial index and, as the view is written, there cannot be one.

| query | time |
|---|---|
| A. `occurrence_days`, one month, no region (today's calendar) | **169 ms** |
| B. same month + Salish Sea bbox | **75 ms** |
| C. Salish Sea bbox with NO day filter (whole corpus) | **3,448 ms** |
| D. bbox on `maplify.sightings` base table (`&&` envelope) | 20 ms (seq scan, 39.6k rows) |
| E. bbox on `inaturalist.observations` base table | 11 ms (seq scan, 20.6k rows) |

**Adding the region makes the calendar query faster, not slower** (169 -> 75 ms). The bbox cuts rows before they reach the view's nested-loop joins against taxa/providers/collections/organizations, which are seq-scanned per row -- the maplify branch alone reports 5.8M "Rows Removed by Join Filter". Those joins, not the spatial predicate, are what the month query actually spends its time on.

**There is no spatial index in prod.** 74 indexes across public/maplify/inaturalist/happywhale; zero GiST, zero on any `location` column.

**An index would not help anyway, for two independent reasons:**
1. `public.occurrences.location` is not a geography -- it is a computed composite, `row(gis.ST_X(location::gis.geometry), gis.ST_Y(location::gis.geometry))::lon_lat`. Any predicate against the view's `location` is an expression over the base column and can never use an index on it. Using one would mean pushing the predicate into the base tables, inside the view or inside a function.
2. The Salish Sea bbox matches **38,272 of 61,389 rows (62%)**. At that selectivity the planner would choose a seq scan over a GiST index regardless.

**Do not add a spatial index as part of this work.** It would be dead weight at this corpus size. Revisit if the corpus grows an order of magnitude or if regions become polygons (design item 2), where `ST_Intersects` against a real shape is a genuinely more expensive predicate.

**Row C is the trap to avoid:** any region query that omits a date bound costs ~3.5 s. Every code path that filters by region must also bound the day.

---

## RESOLVED 2026-07-30: PostgREST can filter the composite. No RPC needed for map or list.

Tested against a full production mirror in the local stack (`scripts/pull-prod-db.sh`). The earlier worry that `location` being a composite rather than jsonb would force everything through RPC functions was **wrong**.

**`->` works and is exact.** A four-sided bbox via the REST API returned `Content-Range: 0-0/38275`, matching `SELECT count(*)` in SQL for the same bbox exactly (38,275):

```
/rest/v1/occurrences?select=id
  &location->lon=gte.-126&location->lon=lte.-122
  &location->lat=gte.47&location->lat=lte.50.5
```

In supabase-js: `.gte('location->lon', -126).lte('location->lon', -122)` and likewise for `lat`.

**`->>` is a silent trap. Do not use it.** The same query with `->>` returned `Content-Range: */0` -- zero rows, no error. `->>` yields text, so the bounds compare lexically instead of numerically and quietly match nothing. Worth a comment at the call site.

**Consequence for scope:** the map query and the observation list need NO migration -- plain PostgREST filters on `from('occurrences')`. Only the calendar needs a schema change, because `occurrence_days` aggregates and the bbox must apply before the `GROUP BY`; the view exposes only `day` and `occurrence_count`, so there is nothing for a client-side predicate to bite on. That is a function taking bbox arguments, and it is the ONLY database work this issue requires. Design item 3 stands as written.

title: CI runs two different Supabase CLI versions
description:
build.yml starts the database with the CLI that supabase/setup-cli puts on PATH (pinned 2.53.6), but 'npm run gen-types' resolves node_modules/.bin/supabase first — the devDependency (2.107.0). So the DB is started by one CLI and its types generated by another, and neither is obviously the intended one.

This is what made salish-cr0's sibling bug hard to see: setup-cli exports SUPABASE_INTERNAL_IMAGE_REGISTRY=ghcr.io and 2.53.6 honours it for 'db start', while 2.107.0 ignored it for 'gen types' (supabase/cli#5785) and pulled postgres-meta from public.ecr.aws, hitting the 1 pull/sec anonymous limit.

deploy.yml also uses setup-cli 2.53.6 for 'supabase link', 'functions deploy' and 'db push' against production, so any unification has to weigh bumping the CLI that runs prod migrations.
design: Options: (a) drop setup-cli from build.yml and use npx supabase everywhere, setting SUPABASE_INTERNAL_IMAGE_REGISTRY=ghcr.io explicitly since that env var is currently a setup-cli side effect; (b) bump setup-cli's pin to match the devDependency. (a) gives one version and makes the registry choice explicit; (b) is smaller but leaves two sources of truth.
acceptance_criteria: A single Supabase CLI version is used across build.yml, and the version is traceable to one place.

title: Inner joins in the DwC export can silently drop occurrence records

title: Emit edge-handler build output outside the source tree (stop shipping tests to Lambda@Edge)

Acceptance: cdk synth succeeds; the synthesized Lambda asset excludes test files and .ts sources; edge-handler jest suite still green. Add a check (test or synth assertion) that the asset contains index.js and not *.test.*.

title: Retire or replace the last in-DB HTTP functions (HappyWhale)
description:
Three in-database functions still make live HTTP calls from Postgres:

- `happywhale.fetch_species_config`
- `happywhale.ensure_species`
- `happywhale.ensure_inat_taxa`

They are the last of the pattern decision 011 set out to remove — Postgres keeps storage and pure relational views, ingest lives in a TypeScript imperative shell.

## Why they were left behind

Migration `20260731120000` retired the equivalent Maplify and iNaturalist functions (salish-89d.3). These were deliberately not included, because HappyWhale was **never part of that cutover**:

- `ingest.runs` has no `happywhale` rows at all — 7,053 iNaturalist runs and 7,091 Maplify runs, zero HappyWhale.
- No cron job has ever scheduled them.
- There is no TypeScript replacement to move the work to.

So dropping them would remove the only mechanism, dormant as it is, with nothing standing behind it. That is a different decision from retiring a path that has a proven replacement running in production, and it belongs in its own change.

Prod does hold HappyWhale data (~5,600 encounters, ~176 kB of individuals), so it was populated at some point — presumably by hand. Whether that data is still wanted, and whether it should be refreshed at all, is the actual question here.

## What to decide first

1. **Is HappyWhale still a source we want?** Check `docs/data-provenance.md` and the rights position before building anything. If the answer is no, this is a deletion, not a migration.
2. If yes, port the fetch into `supabase/functions/ingest` alongside `fetch-maplify.ts` and `fetch-inaturalist.ts`, give it an `ingest.runs` source, and only then drop the three functions.
3. Either way, `supabase/seed.sql` no longer calls `fetch_species_config` — nothing depends on these today.
acceptance_criteria:
- A decision is recorded on whether HappyWhale remains a source.
- If retained: the fetch lives in supabase/functions/ingest, writes an ingest.runs row, and is scheduled the same way Maplify and iNaturalist are.
- The three happywhale.* HTTP functions are dropped in a migration.
- No function in any schema makes an outbound HTTP call from Postgres.

title: Integrate Flukebook (Wildbook) for computer-vision individual identification
description:
WHY: Photo-ID by eye doesn't scale. Flukebook — the Wildbook-based CV photo-ID platform for whales/dolphins — can match a sighting's photos to known individuals automatically, turning every photographed occurrence into a candidate identification. A differentiating, 'killer' feature.

WHAT: Submit occurrence photos to Flukebook's matching API; receive ranked candidate individual matches with confidence scores; record them as candidate Identifications against public.individuals. Flukebook individual IDs map to our catalog as an external-catalog link (alongside HappyWhale). CV match scores are a natural input to the validation model (salish-ek3): high-confidence matches may auto-validate, others stay candidate for human review.

SPIKE / OPEN QUESTIONS (resolve before build):
- Wildbook/Flukebook API capabilities: species coverage (SRKW, Bigg's/transients, humpback), submission + async match-result model, auth, rate/cost.
- Two-way? Whether we also contribute photos/encounters back to Flukebook.
- Cross-catalog dedup: HappyWhale is already mirrored; avoid representing the same animal as two unlinked catalog individuals.

DEPENDS ON the individuals catalog; produces candidate Identifications that feed the identification + validation model.
design:
Two viable architectures (research: docs/research/flukebook-wildbook-api.md):
(A) Contribute INTO hosted Flukebook — request a free account, push encounters/photos via web submit or spreadsheet Bulk Import, let Flukebook's pipeline match, read results back via the login-gated read-only /rest/ query API (what RWildbook wraps). No public 'POST photo → poll for match JSON' endpoint exists on flukebook.org; write access + results at that level need a data-sharing conversation with Wild Me / Conservation X Labs. Data model: 'all data rights remain with contributor' (no CC auto-licensing).
(B) Self-host Wildbook + WBIA (both AGPL) and call WBIA's async job engine directly (/api/engine/query/..., jobid + poll/callback). Full CV control; ops + infra cost.
Either way the match model is async (queue/poll), never request/response.
acceptance_criteria: Photographed occurrences receive ranked candidate individual matches from Flukebook, recorded as candidate identifications with source + confidence score, mapped to public.individuals via a Flukebook external-catalog link.
notes: PARKED 2026-07-03: research complete (docs/research/flukebook-wildbook-api.md), but actual integration is significant product work — not being pursued now. Dominant next action when picked up is a single Wild Me / CXL conversation (orca accuracy + v4 access/licensing + integration path); a draft outreach exists in session history. Deprioritized P2→P3 to match the rest of the individuals epic as unscheduled future work.

title: Define validation model for individual identifications
description: WHY: Identifications differ in trust — a sighter's tag, a regex-extracted candidate (T065S), and a HappyWhale-confirmed match are not equivalent. Per docs/rights-policy.md only validated identities may be emitted as organismID. WHAT: Design the validation/confidence model over identification links (states, who/what validates, provenance of the assertion). Orthogonal to the catalog and linking mechanics — plenty to discuss. Gates organismID emission (salish-1bb).
acceptance_criteria: A documented validation model distinguishing validated from candidate identifications, sufficient to gate organismID emission.

title: Identify individuals in upstream records
description: WHY: Most volume comes through upstream sources; we want their records associated with catalog individuals too. WHAT: Resolve the two upstream inputs against public.individuals — (a) public.extract_identifiers candidate codes parsed from Maplify/native comment text, and (b) happywhale.encounters.individual_id (already a confirmed upstream match). Produce identification links for upstream occurrences. Per decision 008, resolution translates upstream signals into our catalog; it does not adopt the mirror as authoritative. Validation status is handled separately.
acceptance_criteria: Upstream occurrences (maplify/inaturalist/happywhale) carry identification links to catalog individuals where a resolvable identifier or HappyWhale match exists.

title: Identify individuals in our own observations
description: WHY: Native sighters/editors should be able to say which catalog individual(s) an observation records — the primary way our own high-quality identifications enter the system. WHAT: An identification link between a native occurrence (public.observations) and one or more public.individuals, plus the editor UI to set it. Depends on the individuals catalog.
acceptance_criteria: A native observation can be linked to one or more catalog individuals via the editor; the link is queryable on the occurrence.

title: Model an authoritative catalog of individual whales (public.individuals)
description:
WHY: We want our own domain concept of an individual animal — distinct from the happywhale.individuals upstream mirror and from the regex-extracted text identifiers (public.extract_identifiers). Per decision 008 those are INPUTS, not our catalog; their vocabulary must not become our domain.

WHAT: An authoritative public.individuals catalog: stable designation (e.g. T065A), aliases, species, matriline/pod (for SRKW), and links to external catalogs (HappyWhale individual id, etc.). This is the foundation the identification work and organismID emission build on.

Inputs to reconcile into the catalog: happywhale.individuals (~693 mirrored) and public.extract_identifiers output (unvalidated candidate codes like T065S). Validation of identifications is tracked separately (orthogonal).
